test_title: PYST 13: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 16th_September_2025_Shift_1)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements:

1) Both the Prime Minister (PM) and Chief Minister (CM) can advise dissolution of the respective Lower House.

2) Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under Article 356 of the Constitution.

Which of the statements is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Both the **Prime Minister (PM)** and the **Chief Minister (CM)** can advise the dissolution of their respective Lower Houses. **Correct.**

 
 
• The **Prime Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **President** to dissolve the **Lok Sabha** under **Article 85** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the **Chief Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **Governor** to dissolve the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** of the state.
 
• The President and Governor generally act on the aid and advice of their respective Councils of Ministers.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under **Article 356** of the Constitution. **Incorrect.**
 
 
• **President's Rule** is imposed by the **President of India** under **Article 356** when a state's constitutional machinery fails.
 
• The recommendation is generally made by the **Union Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister, and is often based on a report from the **Governor** of the concerned state.
 
• The Constitution does not provide that the **Prime Minister alone** can recommend President's Rule.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, only Statement 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74** provides that the **President** shall act in accordance with the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Article 163** provides that the **Governor** acts on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister**, except in matters where the Constitution grants discretionary powers.
 
• **Article 356** deals with the imposition of **President's Rule** in a state if the constitutional machinery fails.
 
• During **President's Rule**, the powers of the state government are assumed by the **President**, and the state legislature may be suspended or dissolved.
 
• The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within **two months** from the date of its issuance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The landmark **S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994)** judgment placed significant restrictions on the arbitrary use of **Article 356**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the Lower House at the Union level, while the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** is the Lower House at the state level.
 
• The power to dissolve the Lower House is exercised formally by the **President** or **Governor**, but usually on the advice of the elected executive.
